title: Glass at the Glassblower’s Bench
description: Explore ordinary glassmaking vocabulary through heat, recycled fragments, and shaping tools.
cardDescription: Explore ordinary glassmaking vocabulary through heat, recycled fragments, and shaping tools.
focus: Common glass is formed from a heated mixture and shaped before controlled cooling. The clues distinguish the ingredients, the softened material, and the process used to reduce internal stress.
solvingTip: Use whether a clue asks for material, temperature state, tool, or cooling process.
words: To heat and cool glass under control to reduce internal stress
Major glass-forming compound in ordinary sand-based glass
Measured mixture of raw ingredients prepared for a glass furnace
Hollow tube used to shape hot glass with air
High-temperature enclosure used to melt glass ingredients
Melted and capable of flowing, as hot glass may be
Portion of hot glass collected on a working tool
Usually noncrystalline solid forming familiar transparent vessels
Granular source of silica used in common glassmaking
Gas blown through a tube to expand hot glass
Long narrow tool supporting or shaping a glass piece
Thermal energy used to soften glass material
Gas-filled space inside an expanding glass form
Outer form given to a finished glass object

answerNotes.ANNEAL: Annealing uses a controlled temperature cycle; it is different from simply making a glass object colder as fast as possible.
answerNotes.CULLET: Cullet is reusable glass material, distinct from the raw mineral ingredients in a batch.
answerNotes.SILICA: Silica is important in common glass, though not every specialized glass has the same composition.
answerNotes.BATCH: Batch names the prepared mixture rather than the finished object or the furnace itself.
answerNotes.BLOWPIPE: A blowpipe delivers air into the softened glass; solid rods perform other supporting or shaping jobs.

title: Fibers in a Sheet of Paper
description: Follow papermaking through its wet fiber mixture, screen, and the edges of the finished sheet.
cardDescription: Follow papermaking through its wet fiber mixture, screen, and the edges of the finished sheet.
subtheme: Fibers in a Sheet of Paper
focus: Paper forms from fibers arranged and bonded into a sheet. The clues distinguish the plant-derived material from the wet pulp and the equipment used to remove water.
solvingTip: Use the stage described: loose fiber, wet mixture, supported sheet, or pressed result.
words: Plant structural substance forming much ordinary paper fiber
Wet mixture of separated fibers used to form paper
Frame controlling the edge of a handmade paper sheet
One slender strand contributing to a paper sheet's structure
Absorbent support used when pressing many handmade papers
Device squeezing water from a newly formed paper sheet
Liquid carrying the fibers during sheet formation
Single flat piece of paper after forming
Preferred direction of fibers in many machine-made papers
Boundary of a finished paper sheet
Large continuous form used to store machine-made paper
Raw plant material supplying many papermaking fibers
Cloth source of fibers for some papers
Mesh surface on which a wet paper sheet forms

answerNotes.CELLULOSE: Cellulose is a carbohydrate in plant cell walls, not the same material as starch used in some paper treatments.
answerNotes.PULP: Pulp is the fiber mixture before it becomes a dried sheet.
answerNotes.DECKLE: A deckle helps form the sheet boundary; a naturally uneven deckled edge differs from a later straight trim.
answerNotes.FIBER: Individual fibers overlap within the sheet; they are not woven like an ordinary cloth.
answerNotes.FELT: A papermaking felt supports and helps remove water from a wet sheet.

title: Clay Before and After the Kiln
description: Explore ceramic materials through clay mixtures, first firing, and the surface applied to a pot.
cardDescription: Explore ceramic materials through clay mixtures, first firing, and the surface applied to a pot.
subtheme: Clay Before and After the Kiln
focus: A clay body and its glaze are different mixtures. The clues identify a liquid clay suspension, a fired intermediate stage, and the equipment that supplies the high heat.
solvingTip: Separate a material from the heating process or the object being made.
words: Pale clay mineral material associated with porcelain bodies
Pottery after an initial firing and before a later glaze firing
Liquid suspension of clay particles in water
Crushed previously fired ceramic material added to some clay bodies
High-temperature enclosure used to fire pottery
Surface mixture fired to form a glassy coating on pottery
Fine mineral material shaped into an unfired pot
To transform a clay piece by heating it in a pottery kiln
Prepared clay mixture forming a ceramic object's main material
Pyrometric ___, heat-work indicator used in ceramic firing
Hollow ceramic vessel shaped from clay
Rounded open vessel made by a potter
Gripping attachment added to a mug
Upper edge around a ceramic vessel's opening

answerNotes.KAOLIN: Kaolin is an important porcelain ingredient, while a complete clay body can contain other materials.
answerNotes.BISQUE: Bisque names a fired stage; it is different from unfired clay or a finished glaze surface.
answerNotes.SLIP: Slip contains clay particles rather than being simply a transparent coating.
answerNotes.GROG: Grog modifies a clay mixture; it is distinct from dry unfired clay powder.
answerNotes.KILN: A kiln changes ceramic materials through heat; it differs from a household drying cupboard.

title: Wood Viewed Along and Across the Grain
description: Compare wood surfaces through growth rings, knots, and thin layers used in manufactured boards.
cardDescription: Compare wood surfaces through growth rings, knots, and thin layers used in manufactured boards.
subtheme: Wood Viewed Along and Across the Grain
focus: Wood looks different across and along its fibers. The clues distinguish a cut orientation from a growth feature and from a product assembled from thin wood layers.
solvingTip: Use whether the clue describes direction, natural growth, or a manufactured layer.
words: Wood surface cut across the fibers, with spaces omitted
Younger outer wood that conducts water in a tree
Older inner wood formed toward the center of many trunks
Thin layer of wood used as a surface or in layered products
Board made by bonding wood layers with alternating grain directions
Wood feature at the place where a branch joined the trunk
Growth band visible on a crosscut trunk
Outer tree covering removed from many lumber products
Long relatively flat piece of sawn wood
Narrow side of a rectangular board
Broad surface of a sawn board
Cutting tool used to divide timber into pieces
Central material within a layered wood panel
Fibrous material obtained from tree stems
Long substantial member used to support a structure

answerNotes.ENDGRAIN: End grain reveals the cut ends of fibers; it looks different from a lengthwise face.
answerNotes.SAPWOOD: Sapwood is a natural tissue region, not a coating added at a woodworking bench.
answerNotes.HEARTWOOD: Heartwood differs from sapwood in function and often in appearance, though species vary.
answerNotes.VENEER: A veneer is a thin sheet, distinct from a thick solid board.
answerNotes.PLYWOOD: Alternating layer directions help distinguish plywood from a single solid plank.
answerNotes.KNOT: A knot records a growth connection rather than necessarily being a crack or fastening.

title: Familiar Metals and Alloys
description: Compare common metals and their mixtures through familiar material names and manufacturing words.
cardDescription: Compare common metals and their mixtures through familiar material names and manufacturing words.
focus: An alloy combines a metal with other elements. The clues identify traditional compositions while recognizing that modern materials can include additional ingredients and variations.
solvingTip: Use the named combination of elements before choosing a finished-object or process word.
words: Metallic material combining a metal with one or more other elements
Iron-based alloy commonly containing a controlled amount of carbon
Tin-rich alloy used for decorative and household objects
Soft silvery metal forming most traditional pewter
Metal combined with copper to make ordinary brass
Metal forming the principal base of steel
Reddish metal shared by traditional brass and bronze
Silvery metal used in many alloys and coatings
Iron-corrosion product often appearing reddish brown
Natural material from which a useful metal can be extracted
Cast block of metal prepared for later working
To form metal by pouring molten material into a mold

answerNotes.ALLOY: An alloy can include nonmetal elements as well as metals; steel is an example containing carbon.
answerNotes.BRASS: Brass is distinguished from traditional tin bronze by zinc as a principal added element.
answerNotes.BRONZE: Bronze now describes a broader set of copper alloys too; copper and tin identify the classic composition in this clue.
answerNotes.STEEL: Steel differs from pure iron; its properties depend on composition and processing.
answerNotes.PEWTER: Pewter is mainly tin, while additional constituents have varied across periods and products.
